node_definition.done_when: Done when tests/test_a_plan_write_keeps_the_ledger_index.py runs on a temporary crew home holding a ledger of at least 50 runs. Every lookup it measures is of a run id with no run file, which is the case the profile shows. A finished run that has not been promoted has no run file, so has_row (reckon/crew/open_run_index.py:654) passes its file check and reaches _ensure. The test brings the ledger index current and then writes a plan through _store.write_plan. It asserts that the next has_row for such an id returns False and calls ledger.load zero times, counted through a recording stand-in. A second test writes one run through the ledger's own write path, then asserts that the next has_row for a different run id with no run file returns False and calls ledger.load zero times, because the write published its row to the index. Negative control: at the base revision the plan write makes the first test's has_row call ledger.load once. The test files importing the changed modules add no failure against base in matched arms run as an all_debug partition job, submitted with env -u SLURM_JOB_ID -u SLURM_JOBID sbatch and never on the fleet node. Each arm's log sits under the run directory, opens with its revision and literal command, and ends in EXIT=. ruff check and ruff format --check add no finding on the staged paths.
node_definition.goal: Give the ledger its own write generation so a plan write does not invalidate the ledger index
node_definition.negative_control: the base revision, where a plan write makes the next has_row for a run id with no run file call ledger.load
